1.1 What is Civilization ?

🌟“Culture”

1） Definition of Culture (p.1/2)

“Culture is the way of life, especially the general customs and beliefs, of a particular group of people at a particular time."——From the Cambridge Dictionary 

2）Word Root of Culture (p.2)

It originated from the Latin word, cultus, which refers to cultivating or refining something.

🌟 Definition of Civilization （p.1/2）

	(p.1) It is the broadest cultural identity, a collection of cultural characteristics and phenomena that includes language, history, religion, custom, social values, politics, economics, science, culture and art, as well as the self-identification of people 

	(p.1)  "Culture or civilization, taking its broad, ethnographic sense, is that complex whole which includes knowledge, belief, art, morals, law, and any other capabilities and habits by men as a member of society or country."
——From Edward Bennett Tylor, "In Primitive Culture", 1871






	 (p.2) Civilization is "Human society with its well developed social organizations or the culture and the way of life of the society or country at a particular period in time"
——From the Cambridge Dictionary 

	 (p.2) "The highest cultural grouping of people and the broadest level of cultural identity people have short of that which distinguishes humans from other species" 
——From Samuel P Huntington, "the Clash of civilization", 1993 

	(p.2) ”Civilizations are the biggest 'we' within which we feel culturally at home as distinguished from all the other 'them' out there.“——From Samuel P Huntington

It was derived from the Latin term, civis, "someone who resides in a town".

The Number of Civilizations in the Post–Cold War World (Huntington, p. 3) 🌟


According to Huntington, the post–Cold War world is divided into several major civilizations, each defined primarily by shared religion, history, culture, and civilizational identity, rather than by ideology or political systems.

The Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations 
15 May 2019, President Xi: “It is foolish to believe that one's race and civilization are superior to others, and it is disastrous to willfully reshape or even replace other civilizations”.

Think Tank Forum on Mutual Learning Among Asian Civilizations and Building a Community With a Shared Future for Mankind. 

My speech The World Need Dialogue Not Clash.  Shanghai Daily. 
Attitude of Superiority
1793 Macartney. Kowtow.  Qianlong  “The Celestial Empire is abundant for everything. We don’t need trade barbarian goods”. 
Uses this attitude as an excuse to conquer and convert others that will be disastrous. Western colonization. God, Gold and Glory.  
Huntingdon “the West won the world not by the superiority of its ideas or values or religion (to which few members of other civilizations were converted) but rather by its superiority in applying organized violence. Westerners often forget this fact; non-Westerners never do.”

Modernization is not Westernization
Francis Fukuyama “the end of history is the end point of mankind's ideological evolution and the universalization of Western liberal democracy as the final form of human government. There is only one way for all the country that is the Western democracy because it is universal”.
Huntingdon. Clash of civilization. Worry of the decline of the West and the rising of the East. A meaningful warning and a new paradigm.  “What I expect is that my efforts to raise awareness of the dangers of the clash of civilizations will help to promote dialogue among civilizations throughout the world." 
“If non-Western societies are to modernize, they must do it their own way not the Western way”.

My dream of a roundtable meeting
Jesus Christ, Shakyamuni, Confucius, Plato, the Prophet Muhammad. 
A very nice and wise dialogue instead of fighting each other. They have differences but they all taught about love, peace, kindness and tolerance. 

We still have so many conflicts. To coexist we need dialogue among civilizations. The principle of dialogue: to listen, learn, appreciate, 
not to convert, convince, influence. 
Not about how right and beautiful you are, it is about how right and how beautiful the others are.

Samuel Huntington
Clash of Civilizations
Cultural and religious identities will be the primary source of conflict. Two Clashes: West and Islamic, West and Sinic/Chinese. 
Joseph Nye. Soft Power 🌟 [p.8]
Ability to achieve one's goals not by force but by diplomacy, persuasion and the attraction of culture and political value. 
Sharp Power. demonized China and Russia using media and cultural activities to influence public opinion around the world.

Why teach in English
Walking Stick Dependency Syndrome.
Intermediate level. CET band 4. Going further seems very difficult. 
Selinker’s Interlanguage theory. Fossilization. 
The progress of learning stopped, fossilized.  Your English is a mixture of Chinese and English. Our brain has enough room for two languages stored and operate separately. Computer and cell phone can work in Chinese or English but never bilingually. You can’t always rely on Chinese to help your English. Walking Stick is Chinese.  You don’t need a stick to walk. Get rid of it.
Your English is good enough to take this class.

How to study?
1. Before watching, read the subtitles and check the new words
2. Study the key words and questions. You need a notebook to write
   down the definitions of the key words and answers of the questions
3. Finish all the exercises on time

Three Suggestions

1. Read classics
Iliad and  Odyssey, Marcus Aurelius Meditation, Machiavelli the Prince, Thomas More Utopia, Jean-Jacques Rousseau Confessions, Bertrand Russell A History of Western Philosophy.   
Let Plato be your friend, and Aristotle, but more let your friend be truth. 
In the university the most important thing is to get you in touch with what the greatest minds have thought. 
the Harvard Classics. a 51-volume anthology of classic works recommended by the Harvard University president Eliot in 1909.

It is shameful to read English books in Chinese translation if you have been learning English for more than 10 years
